move: dot punches in, stretches into rule, lines rise, kerning tightens, retract
how: A near-black 1080 square with an SVG turbulence grain overlay, a small header row, three 150px uppercase lines (the middle one lime) in masked rows, a thin rule and two footer lines. A lime dot scales in from 0 (expo.out, first 12%) and fades as the rule grows scaleX 0 to 1 from the left (expo.out, 0.7s, at 17%); the lines rise yPercent 110 to 0 with a 0.09s stagger (expo.out, 0.8s, at 18%), then the footer lines and header fade in. From 43% to 83% letter-spacing tightens from -0.045em to -0.06em (sine.inOut). At 78% the lines exit yPercent -110 staggered (expo.in), the footer follows, the rule retracts to the right and the header fades.
adapt: Change the three lines, the accent colour, the header and footer strings; keep the dot-to-rule handoff at 17% and the 0.09s stagger.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the grid of rows and the SVG grain; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with the rule at 0.17D, lines at 0.18D, exit at 0.78D. Scope selectors to el; direct port.
caveats: full-frame feTurbulence grain is expensive to composite every frame
